documents.title: Sample AI Syllabus Policy Statement
documents.summary: A sample syllabus statement from the Center for Teaching and Learning. It treats AI-assisted submissions as academic dishonesty unless the instructor gives express permission, and sets disclosure, citation, supplement-only use, verification and ask-when-unsure rules for approved use.
documents.stance_why: "students are to refrain from using AI tools in this course unless with the express permission of the instructor" bans AI by default and allows it only with instructor approval, so the stance is restrict, although it is a template instructors adopt.

units.why: The opening sentence classifies generative-AI submissions as "forms of academic dishonesty", which sets unauthorized AI use as misconduct (P36) rather than a default-stance rule; the stance itself is coded in the next unit.
units.resolution_why: A coded must-not, B informs; both P36, same actor and phase. The source sentence only classifies AI-assisted submissions as 'forms of academic dishonesty' (a definition of misuse); the prohibition itself is in the next sentence, so modality is informs with unit_stance prohibit.

units.why: "students are to refrain from using AI tools in this course unless with the express permission of the instructor" bans AI unless the instructor explicitly permits it, a default-restrict rule (P01 fits better than P06 because it is the stated default, not a silent-syllabus fallback).
units.anchor: students are to refrain from using AI tools in this course unless with the express
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P01, actor, phase and modality; they differed only on topic (permitted-uses vs academic-integrity). Source: 'refrain ... unless with the express permission of the instructor' is a default ban with exceptions; both topics kept.

units.why: "To maintain a culture of academic integrity" gives the reason for the ban; it explains the rule rather than adding a requirement, so it is rationale.
units.anchor: To maintain a culture of academic integrity
units.frag_end: academic integrity, students are to refrain
units.policy: The restriction on AI tools is meant to maintain a culture of academic integrity.
units.uncovered_note: Integrity-culture rationale for restricting AI; not about skill-building (P41) or an institution-wide framework (P56).
units.resolution_why: Found only by A (kept). Source: 'To maintain a culture of academic integrity' gives the reason for the restriction; it is a stated rationale not covered by an existing type, so UNCOVERED is kept.

units.why: "In those situations when the instructor has approved the use of AI" places the permission decision with the individual instructor, which is P04.
units.anchor: In those situations when the instructor has approved the use of AI
units.frag_end: the following guidelines are in place
units.policy: AI use is allowed only in situations where the instructor has approved it, and the listed guidelines apply in those situations.
units.resolution_why: A anchored 'In those situations when the instructor has approved the use of AI' (course-start, informs); B anchored 'unless with the express permission of the instructor' (during-work, may). Same passage, both P04, actor instructor. The source is a syllabus statement communicating that the instructor decides approval, so phase is course-start; the instructor is empowered to approve, so modality is may.

units.why: "Provide transparency about the use of any AI tool by disclosing that this tool has been used" requires disclosure of AI use with the submission (P24).
units.anchor: Provide transparency about the use of any AI tool by disclosing
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P24, actor, phase, modality. They differed on unit_stance (A permit, B require); the source makes disclosure a condition of instructor-approved use, so permit.

units.why: "as a supplement to and not a replacement for one's own work" keeps the student as the primary producer; closest is P32 (student remains primary problem-solver), and P19 does not fit because it does not ban generation outright.
units.anchor: Use such tools as a supplement to and not a replacement for one’s own work
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P32 and the main codes; unit_stance differed (A permit, B restrict). Source says use tools 'as a supplement to and not a replacement' as a condition of approved use, so permit.

units.why: "including (a) the prompt or prompts ... (b) the name of the tool ... (c) the date ... (d) the associated URL" requires citations to list prompt, tool, date and URL, matching P25.
units.anchor: including (a) the prompt or prompts provided to the tool, (b) the name
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P25 and the main codes; unit_stance differed (A permit, B require). Citation is a condition of approved use, so permit.

units.why: "double-checking and verifying the accuracy of any content generated" with awareness of "biases and errors" requires verifying AI output (P31); the bias mention is secondary to the verification duty.
units.anchor: double-checking and verifying the accuracy of any content generated by using this tool
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P31 and the main codes. B added topic bias, which fits since the source names 'biases and errors'; kept. unit_stance differed (A permit, B require); verification is a condition of approved use, so permit.

units.why: "Seek assistance from the course instructor when in doubt" tells unsure students to ask the instructor, which is P10.
units.anchor: Seek assistance from the course instructor when in doubt about how
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on all main codes; 'Seek assistance from the course instructor when in doubt' fits P10, should, neutral.

notes: Reconciled. Only one included document (CTL sample syllabus statement); library guide excluded in screening. No NEIU-wide, school or computing policy found. Coder B noted AGENT_BRIEF.md topic codes were unavailable to it.
